name: Aveda

lead: Aveda is an American cosmetics company based in Minneapolis, founded by Horst Rechelbacher in 1978 and now owned by Estée Lauder Companies. It makes hair care, hair colour, skin care, body care and cosmetics.
People use its salon products to look better in the everyday ways hair products do: cleaner scalp, hydrated and styled hair, and colour care. Forum posters mention it among preferred hair brands.

paras: Customers buy it at salons and Aveda stores. Users on forums mention specific items such as a cleanser exfoliant, leave-in conditioners and a chemical-removing shampoo sold for swimmers.
Like any cosmetic, scented products can irritate sensitive skin or scalp. No studies compare Aveda with other brands.

angle.text: It is a hair-care and styling brand used to keep hair looking clean and styled. Its salons also offer colour and cuts.

lead: Aveda is an American cosmetics company headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Horst Rechelbacher founded it in 1978 and made the first product, a clove shampoo, by hand in his kitchen sink.[1] Estée Lauder Companies bought the brand in 1997 for $300 million and it operates as a semi-autonomous unit.[1]

The line covers hair care, hair colour, skin and body care, cosmetics and perfume.[1] The brand draws on Ayurvedic traditions in its marketing and says it purchases wind energy for its main manufacturing plant.[1] Aveda Institutes teach cosmetology, massage and esthiology in several U.S. and Canadian cities.[1]
On T Nation forums, some posters say they use only Aveda for hair, citing the smell and range for different hair types.[2] No clinical studies on the brand were found.
infobox: Hair, hair colour, skin, body, cosmetics

paras: Rechelbacher launched the brand in 1978, beginning with a hand-made clove shampoo.[1] Estée Lauder acquired it in 1997 for $300 million, and Rechelbacher sold the salon chain to David Wagner at the same time. The salons were formerly known as Horst and Friends and were later renamed Juut Salonspa.[1]
Aveda sells hair, skin and body care, colour, cosmetics and perfume.[1] It runs Aveda Institutes that train students in cosmetology, massage and esthiology.[1]

A T Nation poster recommended Aveda's cleanser exfoliant as a facial product, and another called themself a hair product snob who uses only Aveda and recommended the scents and range.[3][2] Another noted a shampoo meant to neutralise pool chemicals.[4]

In 2009 the BDS campaign listed Aveda as a brand to boycott because of its parent company's chairman, Ronald Lauder, who also chairs the Jewish National Fund; Wikipedia notes the claim needs a non-primary source.[1]
